sounds.title: The buzzy th
sounds.text: When T and H stand together, they make a brand new sound. Stick the tip of your tongue out between your teeth, and gently buzz. You hear it in the, that, this, they, and there.

sounds.title: The puffy h
sounds.text: H is a little puff of air, like when you fog up a window. You hear it at the start of he, his, and have.

sounds.title: The sneaky quiet e
sounds.text: Sometimes an e sits at the end of a word and makes no sound at all. Shh! Like in are and have.

and.tip: And starts like apple. Then finish with n and d.

they.tip: Buzzy T H! Tongue between your teeth and buzz. The e y says ay, like in play.

that.tip: Buzzy T H! Tongue between your teeth and buzz, then say at.

I.tip: I is just one letter, and it says its own name. It is always a big capital letter.

he.tip: Start with a puff of air for h. Then e says its own name.

at.tip: At starts like apple, then a quick t at the end.

are.tip: Are is a tricky word. It sounds just like the letter R. The e at the end stays quiet.

be.tip: Press your lips together and pop them for b. Then e says its own name.

as.tip: As starts like apple. The s at the end buzzes like a bee.

this.tip: Buzzy T H! Tongue between your teeth and buzz, then say is.

his.tip: His sounds like is, with a little puff of air at the start. The s buzzes like a bee.

have.tip: Puff of air for h, then a like apple. Bite your lip and buzz for v. The e stays quiet.
